description:
FILED s470bi (Opus, 2026-09-05) while probing #1084.  PRE-EXISTING, SILENT,
and far wider than the `do FILE` bug that exposed it.

PCL's `open` DECODES UTF-8 BY DEFAULT where perl reads BYTES.
`%p-split-open-mode` returns `:default` for a mode with no `:encoding` layer,
and SBCL's default external format is UTF-8, so every read of a non-ASCII
file measures CHARACTERS where perl measures octets.

REPRO (scratch/s470bi/p1084/r2.pl in the s470bi worktree; the file
scratch/s469bi/p1084/tiny2.pl is 107 bytes and contains one U+2019 in a
comment, one in a string):

    my $f = "./tiny2.pl";
    open my $fh, '<', $f or die;
    my $src = do { local $/; <$fh> };
    print "srclen=", length($src), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  srclen=107
  PCL:          srclen=101      (the six extra octets of the two U+2019s
                                 collapsed into two characters)

Nothing is printed; the program just measures a different length, and any
byte-oriented use (seek/tell arithmetic, pack, a byte count, a checksum, a
re-write of the file) is then wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND length(): a slurped source string handed to `eval`
disagrees with the same text reached through `do FILE` or `require FILE`.
#1084 made those two agree with perl (octets, and `use utf8` decides); the
slurp-and-eval spelling still gives the DECODED text, so `length("â")`
answers 1 where perl and PCL's own `require` answer 3
(scratch/s469bi/p1084/r.pl, the `eval:` line).

FIX SHAPE (untried): perl's default is bytes -- a handle carries the
`:raw`/`:bytes` behaviour unless a layer (`use open`, a `:encoding(...)` in
the mode, `binmode`) says otherwise.  PCL's `open` should therefore open
`:external-format :latin-1` by default, the way #1084's
`%p-read-source-octets` now reads source.  That is a WIDE change (every
handle in every program) and needs the full sweep + the io/ companion leg,
which is why s470bi filed it rather than taking it inside #1084's commit.
Check `use open qw(:std :utf8)` and `binmode $fh, ':encoding(UTF-8)'` keep
working, and that PRINTING a wide character still encodes (perl dies with
"Wide character in print" on a :raw handle -- probe what PCL should do).

=== DONE (s470br) ===
SHIPPED.  A filehandle carries OCTETS unless a layer says otherwise, which is
perl's default; the whole layer model was probed first (7 read shapes + 8 write
shapes vs 5.40.3) and PCL now answers every one identically.

  * `%p-layer-ef` over `%p-split-layers`: layers left to right, the LAST one that
    names a discipline wins (`<:raw:encoding(UTF-8)` decodes,
    `<:encoding(UTF-8):raw` does not).
  * defaults per DIRECTION (`*p-default-in-ef*` / `*p-default-out-ef*`, both
    :latin-1 = one character per octet, the reading #1084 gave SOURCE);
    standard handles keep a per-DESCRIPTOR vector `*p-std-efs*`.
  * `binmode` stopped being a no-op: SBCL has no (setf stream-external-format),
    so an ordinary handle is rebuilt the way %p-line-buffer-if-tty rebuilds
    buffering (dup, new fd-stream, close the original), carrying $| / the
    fork-pipe pid / $. and seeking an input stream back to its LOGICAL position.
  * `use open` is the ONE never-loaded pragma with a runtime effect and emits
    (p-use-open LIST) into the compile phase.  GLOBAL, not lexical --
    docs/not-supported.md names it.
  * THE WRITE SIDE IS PER STRING, NOT PER CHARACTER: perl prints a UTF8-flagged
    SV as its WHOLE UTF-8 encoding, so "\x{e9}\x{2019}" on a byte handle is
    c3 a9 e2 80 99 -- the e-acute becomes TWO octets although one would hold it.
    Using only SBCL's OUTPUT-REPLACEMENT restart (per character, and free) gives
    e9 e2 80 99: one octet short of perl on exactly the common `use utf8` shape.
    So %p-out-string decides the string whole and the restart is the BACKSTOP.
    `syswrite` is perl's one FATAL here and now is PCL's.

TWO REVIEW FIXES the companion legs found (same lesson twice: a repair must not
reach for the thing it repairs):
  1. the encoding handler must REPAIR AND SAY NOTHING -- it warned, the harness
     binds *error-output* to a line-atomic Gray stream, the warning went into the
     same pending buffer as the text that had just failed to encode, and flushing
     it signalled on the same character forever (uni/lex_utf8.t died at
     *MAXIMUM-ERROR-DEPTH*, uni/fold.t lost 928 rows);
  2. binmode must decide by DESCRIPTOR -- `binmode *STDOUT, ':utf8'` hands over a
     TYPEGLOB, which %p-std-slot does not read as a standard-handle name, so the
     rebuild path CLOSED descriptor 1.  New %p-std-descriptor.  %p-std-slot's
     blindness is #1220.

AND ONE MORE THING THE CHANGE FORCED: a byte STDERR makes PCL's OWN diagnostics
fatal (%p-announce-unsupported writes an EM DASH), which cost four rows of
transpile-test-07.t and five of moo-01.t plus ir-inventory.pl's dump.  ONE writer
per audience: %p-diag (runtime stderr), %tap-out (the TAP layer's 25 `format t`
calls), p-load-with-recovery wrapped; a TOOL that wants character output says so.

BARS: gate 209 files / 7104 tests green except the 13 pclxs xs rows; corpus-diff
1 of 111 (magic.t, the only `use open` file), silent drops 5 unchanged;
emission-ab over the 63 `use open` files 61 DIFF / 2 SAME (both `use open` inside
a heredoc / POD) / RCDIFF 0; companion io/+uni/ --jobs 1 = 0 NEW ROW, 14 FIXED
ROW, 0 UNVERIFIED, 0 LOST (io/utf8.t 13/14 -> 23/4 and io/bom.t 0/3 -> 1/2 mine,
confirmed on a `git archive f728637` extraction; uni/gv.t 56/32 -> 59/29 NOT mine
-- the base reads 59/29 too).  Generation v2-791, three artifacts regenerated.
Guard Pl/t/io-layers-01.t (16 rows).  ir-spec Â§7.7 is the normative record.
Filed on the way: #1220, #1221.
subject: PCL's open() decodes UTF-8 by default where perl reads BYTES: every slurp of a non-ASCII file measures characters, not octets (srclen 101 vs perl's 107)
